package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all Volusion-hosted stores compromised in the breach)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment card details from end customers by exfiltrating sensitive data entered on checkout/payment pages to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This constitutes a classic Magecart-style web skimming attack, directly targeting confidential financial information.

execution_context.trigger: At the moment a customer submits payment details on the checkout page (form submission event).
execution_context.file_location: Injected into Volusion-hosted store web pages, typically within <script> tags or as external JavaScript references loaded on checkout/payment pages.
required_permissions: Access to DOM elements (specifically payment input fields)
Ability to attach event listeners to forms
Outbound network access to arbitrary domains

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At form submission on the checkout page, the code attaches an event listener to the payment form, collects payment card details from input fields, encodes the data, and sends it via an image beacon to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive financial information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment card data directly from user input fields and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled domain, which is a clear indicator of web skimming activity and is never legitimate in third-party scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should never access or transmit raw payment card data to external domains. Payment processing must be handled by secure, PCI-compliant APIs, and direct access to card data by third-party scripts is strictly prohibited.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate analytics or fraud detection scripts may monitor form events or anonymized data, but they never collect or transmit full payment card details to untrusted or non-PCI-compliant domains.
key_indicators: Direct access to payment card input fields (e.g., card number, expiry, CVV)
Attachment of event listeners to sensitive forms (e.g., checkout or payment forms)
Outbound network requests (such as image beacons or XHR/fetch) to domains not associated with the legitimate e-commerce provider or payment processor
Encoding or obfuscation of exfiltrated data (e.g., use of base64 encoding via btoa)
Presence of unexpected or unauthorized <script> tags or external JavaScript references on payment pages

attack_chain.action: Attacker breaches Volusion infrastructure and injects malicious JavaScript into customer store pages.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in end-user browsers.

attack_chain.action: Injected JavaScript executes in the context of the checkout/payment page, hooking into form submission events to monitor user input.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card data entered by customers.

attack_chain.action: Collected payment card data is encoded and exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure via outbound network requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment card data for further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code accessing payment card input fields (e.g., input[name="cardnumber"], input[name="expdate"], input[name="cvv"]) on checkout or payment pages
Event listeners (such as 'submit') attached to forms with actions related to checkout or payment
Outbound network requests (XMLHttpRequest, fetch, or image beacons) from checkout pages to domains not associated with Volusion or recognized payment processors
Encoding or obfuscation of data (e.g., use of btoa or base64 encoding) prior to network transmission
Presence of unauthorized or unexpected <script> tags or external JavaScript sources on sensitive pages
file_indicators: Unexpected <script> tags or external JavaScript references present in checkout/payment page HTML
JavaScript code or files not present in the official Volusion codebase or deployment pipeline
References to suspicious, newly registered, or previously unseen domains in script sources or network requests
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout or payment pages to domains unrelated to Volusion or legitimate payment processors
Use of image beacons (e.g., new Image().src) or GET requests with base64-encoded payloads containing sensitive data
Network traffic to domains or IPs known to be associated with Magecart or other web skimming groups
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for unauthorized or unexpected JavaScript modifications on checkout/payment pages, focusing on scripts that access payment input fields and initiate outbound requests to external domains. Deploy web application firewalls (WAFs) and enforce strict content security policies (CSP) to block or alert on suspicious script activity. Regularly scan production environments for new or modified scripts, and monitor network traffic for exfiltration patterns typical of Magecart attacks, such as encoded payloads sent to untrusted domains.
